ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two terminals on the left side of the figure, labeled A and B. A and B are respectively connected to the upper and lower two nodes of the circuit. Between the two nodes there is a middle branch, and on the branch there is only one 10 Ω resistor. On the right outer loop there is also a branch from the upper node to the lower node, passing in sequence through the top 10 Ω resistor, the right-side 10 Ω resistor, and the bottom 10 Ω resistor. Reasoning: The three 10 Ω resistors in the right-side branch of the outer loop are in series, so the equivalent is 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 Ω. The middle branch is a single 10 Ω resistor. Both branches are connected between the two nodes A and B, therefore they are in parallel. The equivalent resistance is Req = (10 × 30) / (10 + 30) = 300 / 40 = 7.5 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit topology visible in the figure: A and B are the two left-side terminals, with a direct middle branch containing a single 10 Ω resistor, and an outer right-hand branch containing three 10 Ω resistors in series.
